Hi Sophia —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, I ran a set of scenarios to help Alder evaluate migrating from monthly/quarterly billing to an annual prepay structure while keeping production risk low. I attached a short spreadsheet that compares three commitment profiles and the associated concessions.

High-level options in the attachment:
- Option A: 12-month prepay — 12% term discount, monthly true-ups, 30% safety credit for first 60 days.
- Option B: 24-month prepay — 18% term discount, staged ramp credits (months 1-3), indexed stepdown for underutilization.
- Option C: 36-month prepay — 24% term discount, larger up-front credit, built-in renewal uplift protection.

As discussed, Alder’s top asks were: minimize PO friction, avoid heavy revenue recognition spikes on your side, and a short safety window to validate production performance. The spreadsheet includes both an amortized cost view for finance and an ops timeline for our infra team.

Can you confirm which scenario you want us to price for your procurement team (we can convert any option to net-30 or net-60 invoice terms if needed)? If helpful, I can introduce our finance lead to walk through the amortization and provide a vendor-friendly invoice schedule.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen\Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophia —

Thanks for the questions. I put together a short annotated summary below and updated the attached PDF with the specific payout/true-up language you asked for. Key clarifications: 

1) Cashflow & recognition (for Option B, 24-month prepay):
   - We can invoice upfront (one invoice) or split into two equal invoices at T0 and T+12 months. For your accounting team, we provide a month-by-month amortization schedule (attached tab: amortization).
   - If you prefer our recommended invoice schedule to limit your cash hit, we suggest 2 invoices (T0, T+12) with monthly expense recognition for your internal reports.

2) DocuSign / T&Cs:
   - DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/rs/4b7a-sign/ALDER-8473
   - Standard enterprise SOW + Data Processing Addendum included in the link. No aggressive indemnity language; typical SOC2 and data residency clauses are present.

3) Safety credit triggers / clawback mechanics:
   - Safety credit is credited as a one-time usage credit applied to invoices for the first 60 days. If your true usage exceeds the prepaid tokens by >40% during months 1–3, we propose a staged step-up where any overage is invoiced at a 30% discount to list for months 2–3, then standard rates thereafter.
   - If actual long-term usage consistently exceeds the prepaid baseline by >50% after the first 6 months, we will propose a true-up to the next tier at a pro-rated rate (this protects both parties).

4) Procurement-friendly invoice cadence options (pick one):
   - A: Upfront single invoice (full prepay) with 30-day payment terms.
   - B: Split prepay (50/50) invoiced at signature and at 12 months.
   - C: Quarterly drawdown (for 24-month only) — invoiced quarterly against prepay balance; requires PO for the full term.

5) Implementation & SLA ramp timeline:
   - Standard 6–8 week onboarding for production traffic. Can accelerate to 4 weeks for an implementation fee.

I attached the updated concession language as Alder_3yr_offer_redwood_terms.pdf and the updated spreadsheet that includes an amortization tab. If you want, Aditya (cc’d) can run a few numeric permutations based on your projected ramp numbers.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop\Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
